panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of open mouth showing grouped vesicles/crusting of lower lip with oral erosions. Caption 'Herpes labialis with oral erosions' and in-text 'multiple grouped vesicles in the peri-oral region along with multiple oral erosions [Figure 3]' in article titled herpes labialis supports herpes_simplex attribution.

in_text_mentions: nder. Hemorrhagic crusting of the lips was also present [Figure 2]. With a provisional diagnosis of recurrent EM due to HSV, the patient was prescribed oral Acyclovir 200 mg 5 times a day for 7 days and topical supportive therapy. Within 2 weeks, the hemorrhagic crusting had regressed and the lesion on the cheek had reduced in size. After 2 weeks of stopping treatment, the patient reported back with multiple grouped vesicles in the peri-oral region along with multiple oral erosions [Figure 3]. Careful examination of the body also revealed a solitary target lesion on the right thigh [Figure 4].

Intranuclear inclusion bodies could be seen in some cases (Figure 3).

in_text_mentions: Cold sores develop via several stages characterized by different symptoms (Figure 1). In the first stage, patients may feel tingling, itching, or a burning sensation, but without the blister being formed yet. plate_findings.evidence: Cowdry bodies and cytologic changes consistent with herpes simplex virus infection (H&E, x600)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Panel-specific caption states Cowdry bodies and cytologic changes consistent with HSV in liver, supported by article title of disseminated intrauterine HSV in 23-week neonate and in-text large multinucleate cells with margination and molding and Cowdry bodies immunopositive for HSV. b: Panel-specific caption identifies liver focus of HSV infection by HSV immunostain; same liver disease process described in-text as having multinucleate cells with margination/molding and Cowdry bodies. c: Panel-specific caption states cardiac papillary muscle foci of HSV infection by immunostain; in-text states myocardium had similar cytopathologic changes and necrosis as liver multinucleate cells. d: Panel-specific caption states skin hair follicle HSV infection by immunostain; in-text states skin had similar cytopathologic changes and necrosis as liver multinucleate cells.
panels.attribution_text: Srivastava et al. Herpes in the Heart: A Case of Widely Disseminated Intrauterine Herpes Simplex Virus Infection Involving Neonatal Myocardium in a 23-Week Gestationally Aged Neonate.. Case reports in infectious diseases 2020. doi:10.1155/2020/1305915. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Liver: (a) Cowdry bodies and cytologic changes consistent with herpes simplex virus infection (H&E, ×600); (b) focus of infection (herpes simplex virus immunostain, ×100). Cardiac papillary muscle: (c) foci of infection (herpes simplex virus immunostain, ×100). Skin: (d) infection of hair follicle (herpes simplex virus immunostain, ×100).
in_text_mentions: s affecting the liver, heart, and skin. The liver lesions revealed numerous areas of necrosis with large, multinucleate cells with margination and molding of their nuclei and Cowdry bodies that were immunopositive for HSV (using an HSV1/HSV2 antibody cocktail) (Figure 2(a)). The skin and myocardium had similar cytopathologic changes and necrosis (Figures 2(c) and 2(d)). The thymus, spleen, stomach, adrenal glands, and lungs also contained foci with weak cytoplasmic immunopositivity for HSV but with minimal cytopathologic changes. There was necrosis of the muscularis propria of the large bowel.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of lower face/oral cavity showing multiple erosions of tongue dorsum and lower lip/vermilion. Article title is HSV-focused and caption plus in-text describe vesicles on erythematous base with erosions extending onto vermilion lip in HSV infection, supporting herpes_simplex attribution. Lip component mapped to herpes_labialis_vesicles vocabulary; extensive tongue/oral erosions recorded as proposed findings. Atypical per title in immunocompromised patient.
panels.attribution_text: Alghamdi et al. Atypical Presentation of Herpes Simplex Virus Infection in an Immunocompromised Patient.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.37465. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Erosions on the tongue and lips
in_text_mentions: n that involved buccal mucosa, palatine, and tongue. It was associated with difficulty swallowing solid and liquid food. The patient did not report skin lesions or the involvement of other mucosal sites. A review of her family history was non-contributory. Clinically, the patient appeared unwell and presented with a group of vesicles on the erythematous base accompanied by a burning sensation, erosions associated with hemorrhagic crusts that extended onto the vermilion lip, as well as painful multiple erosions of the oral mucosa that involved buccal mucosa, palatine, and tongue (Figures 1, 2).
